context: 10 Open Problems Some of the open problems in [7] and [14] still remain open. For rotatable dominoes, one problem that remains open is whether Tetris clearing and survival remain solvable in polynomial time if we assume a different rotation model, such as a version of SRS for dominoes. In our polynomial-time algorithms for Tetris clearing and survival with rotatable dominoes, we assume that the rotation center only moves monotonically downwards. While the algorithm might be able to be adapted to different rotation systems that allow for the rotation center to move upwards, the details are much more tricky, and it is also possible that the problem is NP-hard. For tetromino piece types, the main open problems of interest are the computational complexity of Tetris clearing and survival for pieces. For clearing, while pieces cannot rotate, thus simplifying the problem (as there are no spins involving pieces) and leading us to believe that this is plausibly in P, it is still not straightforward to prove due to the row-clearing mechanic. For survival, we have evidence that suggests that the problem is NP-hard, as 2 × 2 square packing in orthogonally convex grid polygons is NP-hard [2], but there are still a few tricky details to work out, particularly in ensuring that all pieces can be successfully placed under Tetris rules.
